meta.title: x/tools/gopls: diagnostics not cleared when import cycle is resolved
meta.fix_ref: golang/tools@9aa007ed1667 (internal/lsp/cache: invalidate broken packages when imports are deleted; CL 326589)
meta.build_notes: go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@<version> with the local Go (go1.27.1), which builds both; the server runs the local go command. v0.7.0 was tagged 2021-06-08 (a commenter reproduced the bug with v0.7.0), the fix merged 2021-06-10, v0.7.1 was tagged 2021-08-02.
meta.notes: A go list error (the import cycle) became sticky: when the edit deleted the import that closed the cycle, the broken packages were not invalidated, so the cycle error on b/b.go and the 'could not import mod.test/b' error on a/a.go stayed. The fix invalidates packages with errors when imports are deleted.

settings_note: The reporter's editor ran goimports on save; the case applies the edit that goimports makes (deleting the unused import) as a second change, then saves.

repro.steps: Open a/a.go and b/b.go (a and b import each other: import cycle). In b/b.go delete 'const B = a.B' (line 5), then delete the now unused import of mod.test/a (lines 2-3, what goimports does on save) and save. Reported: the cycle is resolved but gopls keeps 'could not import mod.test/b' on a/a.go and 'import cycle not allowed' on b/b.go. Probe: the diagnostics of both files after the edits are compared with a fresh session on the edited files and a fresh control.
